title: Kenansville business celebrates one-year anniversary operating as storefront business - NewsBreak
text:
By Lauren Branch ,
5 hours ago
KENANSVILLE — Thanksgiving is not the only thing a local business is celebrating this November. MJ’s Unique Designs is also celebrating its first anniversary as a storefront business.
Owner Monica James hosted an anniversary celebration from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Nov. 12 at the floral shop located at 162 Liberty Square. During the event, customers had a chance to talk to James and learn more about her business and what she offers, enjoy free refreshments and win prizes.
The Duplin County native had a home-based business for six years before deciding to take a leap of faith to open up a storefront location.
“It took a lot of prayer, guidance and opportunity. My nail tech gave me information about this place I’m in now, and it just went from there,” James said.
According to James, she specializes in creating unique and custom floral arrangements for all occasions, including birthdays, anniversaries and celebrations of life.
“My really, really big thing (is) weddings. That’s really popular for us. It’s our bread and butter,” she explained.
The business idea came around during a time when James was laid off. She decided to keep her head up and look for what was next for her life.
“I mean, I was laid off, and I’m my own person, so I said I would like to have my own money,” she said with a laugh. “So, I just started dabbling in custom shirts, cups, pillows, graphics and things like that. Family members started asking me to plan their weddings. So I started coordinating my family members’ weddings, and it kind of went from there. I found a love and a joy from it.”
Like most people, James’ career path did not turn out exactly like she wanted it to as a child. In her youth, she dreamed of becoming a nurse, a dream she still plans to achieve.
“I wanted to be a nurse. Before I’m 50, I’ll be nurse, but right now this is my joy. It’s my ministry, I feel. So no, this is not what I wanted to be as a child. Literally, all I had to do was take a test to get into the nursing program. But when you pray for your purpose — God was literally like, no, we’re going to do this. He literally did it. Yeah, he did it,” she explained.
James enjoys teaching others how to do what she does. She offers a decorating class in her store to help people learn how to create.
“That’s a part of our business. Right now we have, like, a women’s ministry that comes in. They love it. It’s very therapeutic. It’s really nice, and luckily I am able to cut the cost because I don’t have to get a building. They can just come here,” she said.
The store is open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday-Friday and 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Saturday.
To learn more or to sign up for a class, contact Monica James on Facebook, by phone at 910-242-3950 or by visiting mjsuniquedesignsandevents.com.
